2027-02-20.title: Saturday of the second week of the Great Fast
readings: Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?
The goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior appeared
Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also
2027-02-20.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), second week. Tomorrow is M'shario Sunday, the Sunday of the healing of the paralytic.
2027-02-20.verse: Do not be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
theo: As the guests leave Mamre, Abraham walks with them “to set them on their way,” and the Lord speaks almost to himself: “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?” God treats Abraham as a friend, someone who may know his plans. And he explains why he chose him: “that he may charge his children and his household after him to keep the way of the Lord by doing righteousness and justice.” Faith is meant to be handed on at home, from parents to children, in words and in the way a household lives. Then God speaks of “the outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah.” The cry of those who suffer injustice rises to heaven, and God says: “I must go down and see.” The God of Abraham is not indifferent to the cry of the oppressed.

Paul reminds Titus how a Christian household should look to its neighbours: “to speak evil of no one, to avoid quarreling, to be gentle, and to show every courtesy to everyone.” He does not pretend we were always so: “we ourselves were once foolish, disobedient, led astray… But when the goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior appeared, he saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.” In the Gospel Jesus speaks tenderly to that small, renewed household: “Do not be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom. Sell your possessions, and give alms… For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.” St Augustine urged his people to move their treasure to heaven through the hands of the poor, so that their hearts would follow (in substance). Almsgiving in the Fast is not only charity; it is moving our heart to where God is.
outline: Ask: where does your mind go when you are not thinking of anything in particular?
Charging his household to keep the way of the Lord.
Saved by mercy, renewed by the Spirit.
“Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.”
live: Tonight, read a short passage of Scripture with your children or family and explain it in your own words.
Set aside what you saved by fasting this week and give it to someone in need.
2027-02-20.prayer: God our Savior, you did not hide your plans from Abraham, and you chose him to teach his household your way. Your goodness and loving kindness appeared in Christ, and you renewed us through the water of rebirth. Make our homes schools of righteousness and justice, free us from fear, and draw our hearts to the treasure of your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At the altar the Father gives the little flock the kingdom, in the Body and Blood of his Son.

quick: God chose Abraham to teach his household to do righteousness and justice.
God saved us by his mercy, through the water of rebirth and the Holy Spirit.
Jesus says: do not be afraid, little flock; where your treasure is, there your heart will be.
2027-02-20.action: Give away today what you saved by fasting this week.
2027-02-20.question: Where is my treasure, and so where is my heart?

family.explain: Jesus calls us his little flock and says: do not be afraid. God wants to give us his kingdom. He asks us to share what we have with the poor, because what we give in love is kept safe in heaven.
family.intention: We pray for poor families, and for our family to be generous.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we share this week with someone who has less?”

illus: A schoolboy in Kundara asked his grandfather why the family always ate a plain supper on Saturdays in Lent. The old man took him to a small tin behind the holy pictures. Inside were coins and folded notes, the money saved each week. On Holy Thursday they would take it to an old couple down the road who had no children. The boy asked: why not just give it now? His grandfather said: because every Saturday, when you are hungry, you will remember them. That is how a heart learns where its treasure is.

pm.open: Father, you are pleased to give us the kingdom. Free us from fear and draw our hearts to you. Amen.
share: That he may charge his children and his household (Genesis 18:19). What am I handing on to the next generation?
He saved us... according to his mercy (Titus 3:5). How have I experienced God's mercy this week?
Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also (Luke 12:34). Where is my heart?
interc: For parents and grandparents who hand on the faith at home.
For the victims of injustice whose cry rises to God.
For catechumens preparing for the water of rebirth this Easter.
For the poor who will receive the alms of this Fast.
For our parish as we approach M'shario Sunday.
pm.close: Father, it is your good pleasure to give us the kingdom. Make our homes places of faith, our hearts free from fear, and our hands open to the poor. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the Lord said: shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do? I have chosen him, that he may charge his children and his household after him to keep the way of the Lord by doing righteousness and justice (Genesis 18:17, 19). God trusts Abraham as a friend, and expects faith to be passed on at home.
God also hears the outcry against Sodom: I must go down and see (Genesis 18:20–21). The cry of the oppressed reaches heaven.

Paul says we were once foolish and led astray, but when the goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior appeared, he saved us, according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:3–5). So we are to be gentle and courteous to everyone.

And Jesus says: do not be afraid, little flock. Sell your possessions, and give alms. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also (Luke 12:32–34). As we end this second week of the Fast, let us move our treasure, and our heart, toward God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus calls us his little flock, like little sheep. He says: do not be afraid! God wants to give you his kingdom. When we share our things with poor people, we are storing treasure in heaven. What can you share this week?

intro: Theme: “Do not be afraid, little flock.”
A household that keeps the way of the Lord, a mercy that renews, and a heart that follows its treasure.

q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.
I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, lives in you.
points.apply: Begin or renew family prayer with Scripture every evening of the Fast.

sub: Not by works, but by mercy.
q: The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.
Jesus answered, “Very truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.
points.apply: Be gentle and courteous this week to the person you find hardest to bear.

sub: Purses that do not wear out.
q: Prayer with fasting is good, but better than both is almsgiving with righteousness.
but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consumes and where thieves do not break in and steal.
points.apply: Keep a Lenten alms box at home and give its contents to the poor before Easter.

concl: God entrusts his ways to households that will hand them on.
Where our alms go, our hearts follow.
2027-02-20.resolve: Give each week of the Fast what you have saved by fasting.
